motivering: The Centre Party emphasises that everyone should be able to have their case heard and that lead times for dispute resolution must be shortened. Extending a neutral, independent arbitration procedure to the entire rental market — including the private stock — is consistent with the party's liberal view of market-based and efficient solutions over state micro-management. V's reservation is not in line with the Centre Party's market-liberal principles and is therefore rejected.

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden must be able to have their case heard. The lead times for processing and the exercise of public authority in courts and agencies must be shortened and access to legal counsel improved.

The ability to take legal action against the state or a municipality, when there are good grounds for having one's case heard, must in a liberal democracy not be a right reserved for those with high incomes.
Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services.

motivering: The Centre Party's election manifesto demands that Sweden commit two percent of GDP to defence 'as soon as practically possible' and rapidly and forcefully build up total defence (totalförsvar). The committee has rejected C's own motion 4 (Mikael Larsson et al.), which means Reservation 1 reflects the party's own position. Voting Yes would mean approving the rejection of its own motion, which contradicts the explicit defence commitment. C votes No to support its reservation.

citations.quote: Sweden needs to commit two percent of GDP to defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.
citations.princip: two percent of GDP for defence

citations.quote: We want to build up the military defence rapidly, forcefully, and for the long term.

Russia's invasion, which violates international law, has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defence of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots. The Centre Party wants to build up the defence, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete its entry into NATO.
citations.princip: build up total defence and NATO accession

motivering: The legislative amendment introduces a sustainability objective for the Seventh AP Fund (Sjunde AP-fonden), which directly reflects the Centre Party's climate ambitions. The objective of high-quality pension savings for a secure pension aligns well with the party's commitment to defending the long-term fairness and sustainability of the pension system. The Centre Party would not support the Left Party's (Vänsterpartiet) motion, which likely counteracts market-based flexibility in asset management.

citations.quote: We must defend the long-term fairness and sustainability of the pension system.
The Centre Party puts climate first, because the future must be green.

motivering: The Centre Party explicitly lists the restrictions on freedom it rejects — a restriction on freedom of association for terrorist organisations is not among them. The party emphasises that 'society must not give way' to organised crime and demands more tools throughout the justice chain. The dormant proposal enables — without automatically enforcing — legislation against associations linked to terrorism, which falls within the party's security-policy commitments without violating its explicitly stated liberal limits.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance, and restrictions on freedom of religion.

Society must not give way to the gangs. To defeat them requires better efforts to prevent new recruitment, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts, and the prison and probation service, and stricter sentences.
citations.princip: public safety and the justice chain

citations.quote: We want to make it harder to amend the constitution, protect the position of the opposition in the Riksdag, and strengthen the independence of the courts.

motivering: The Centre Party lacks an explicit position on gambling regulation in its election manifesto. However, the party strongly defends popular movements (folkrörelser) and civil society organisations — which traditionally run lotteries for public benefit — and supports well-functioning consumer protection regulation. The committee's proposal to reject SD's motion 2 is more consistent with C's liberal consumer protection stance and the party's clear principled line of not following SD's political wishes.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats (Sverigedemokraterna) or give them power over how Sweden is governed.
The sports movement and Sweden's popular movements (folkrörelser) make valuable contributions to building trust and community.
citations.princip: support for civil society's popular movements

motivering: The Centre Party strongly emphasises that Sweden must be defended in light of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which makes the criminalisation of foreign espionage directly compatible with the party's security policy. The committee's proposal already rejects the parts concerning Chapter 27, Section 2 (surveillance), which is in line with C's explicit rejection of preventive surveillance. The restrictions on the right to communicate information to the press (meddelarfriheten) create a tension with the party's press-freedom commitment, but national security carries greater weight in this narrowly defined context.

citations.quote: Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion, which violates international law, has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war.
We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
Freedom of the press must be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
citations.princip: freedom of the press must be protected

omvarld.faktor: Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine – Ukrainian forces retake Kherson
omvarld.effekt: Reinforces the application of the party's defence policy and justifies security legislation against foreign espionage

motivering: The Centre Party actively defends labour immigration and emphasises that policy must not let down companies that need to recruit foreign expertise. A raised income requirement is a new restriction that risks excluding categories of labour migrants and runs counter to the party's stated line of making it easier to hire and keeping borders open to mobility. The party should vote no to the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Defend labour immigration. For Swedish companies to be able to compete, they must have the ability to quickly find, recruit, and hire the right expertise.
Policy must not let down all those companies that cannot manage without labour immigration.
It must become cheaper and easier to hire, especially people who are far from the labour market.

motivering: The Centre Party defends the rule of law and wants transparency and order in the exercise of public authority. The proposal strengthens the reliability of coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) through tightened identity checks and a clearer tiered structure, in line with the party's emphasis on legal certainty and combating corruption. Nothing in the documents supports approving V's reservation, which likely aims to weaken identity requirements. The Centre Party votes Yes to the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: must become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.
The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended.
citations.princip: rule of law and legal certainty

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden must be able to have their case heard. The lead times for processing and the exercise of public authority in courts and agencies must be shortened and access to legal counsel improved.
citations.princip: access to fair exercise of public authority

motivering: The Centre Party supports EU cooperation and openness to the wider world, which argues in favour of implementing the EU directive on copyright in the digital single market. The party's emphasis on cultural freedom as a cornerstone of civil society supports strengthened rights for creators. Granting the press the right to compensation for online re-use is consistent with the party's view that independent media coverage is essential to democracy. The committee's proposal to approve the government's bill is therefore in line with the party's principles.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society.
Comprehensive, independent, and vital media coverage across the entire country is essential to democracy.

motivering: The Centre Party has submitted its own motion in the matter (Malin Björk et al., C) and has entered a reservation against the committee majority's proposal to reject it. The party generally supports shorter processing times in the courts but strongly emphasises the principles of the rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state. Voting no means supporting the party's own reservation (alternative A), which is consistent with documented positions.

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden must be able to have their case heard. The lead times for processing and the exercise of public authority in courts and agencies must be shortened and access to legal counsel improved.

The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: principles of the rule of law

motivering: The Centre Party's election manifesto contains explicit commitments to cut waiting times, create more hospital beds through a billion for places (platsmiljard), and defend freedom of choice in healthcare. The committee's proposal to note the written communications — despite the requirements not having been fully met — directly contradicts these priorities. The party should vote No and support reservation 1 to signal that the Riksdag's formal requests (tillkännagivanden) have not yet been fulfilled.

citations.quote: Waiting times must be cut and people must have the right to opt out of queues by seeking care in other regions. We want to create more hospital beds where needed with the help of a billion for places and better support for the regions.
citations.princip: billion for places to create more hospital beds

citations.quote: We want to cut waiting times and create more hospital beds where needed through investments in more nurses and better state support for the regions adapted to their conditions and needs.
citations.princip: more hospital beds and shorter waiting times

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in health and social care and conduct operations close to those receiving care.
citations.princip: freedom of choice in health and social care

motivering: The Centre Party emphasises that independent media coverage is essential to democracy and that freedom of the press must be protected. The party's transparency principle — 'Sweden must become even more transparent' — supports increased insight into the ownership of radio and television companies as a democracy-strengthening tool. The committee's proposal to reject the motion and approve the government's transparency proposal is consistent with these clear values of openness and a free press.

citations.quote: Comprehensive, independent, and vital media coverage across the entire country is essential to democracy. Freedom of the press must be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
Sweden must become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: Centerpartiet has a clear commitment that processing times in courts and public authorities must be shortened and that everyone shall be able to have their case tried. The committee's proposal confirms the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) observations, presupposes the government's follow-up and thereby drives the improvement work the party demands. Approving the committee's proposal and rejecting V's and MP's motions is consistent with C's goals without requiring support for the motioners' specific line.

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden shall be able to have their case tried. Processing times for handling and the exercise of public authority in courts and public authorities must be shortened and access to counsel improved.
The rule of law and the individual's rights against the state must be defended.
citations.princip: defense of the rule of law

motivering: The proposal to criminalize foreign espionage is directly consistent with Centerpartiet's strong commitment to national security and defense against external threats, particularly Russia's ongoing war. The restrictions on the right to communicate information to the media (meddelarfriheten) are narrowly delimited to espionage for a foreign power's account, not general whistleblowing, and appear proportionate in relation to C's press freedom principle. The defense and security argument carries the most weight.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot exclude Sweden being drawn into war.
Comprehensive, independent and viable media coverage throughout the country is crucial for democracy. Press freedom shall be protected and independent public service defended.

The rule of law and the individual's rights against the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance and restrictions on freedom of religion.

motivering: The proposal strengthens identity verification for coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) and reduces the risk of incorrect data remaining in the population register database. Centerpartiet's election manifesto emphasizes that the rule of law shall be defended and that Sweden shall become more transparent with tougher measures against fraud and corruption. These principles support the committee's proposal to reject V's motion, which is why Yes is the right vote.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights against the state must be defended.
citations.princip: principles of the rule of law

citations.quote: Sweden shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: Centerpartiet has submitted its own motion in the matter (claim 2 by Helena Lindahl et al.) which the committee wishes to reject. Reservation 5 corresponds to the party's position and is the option the party should support. The party's liberal core values emphasize individual rights against the state and a restrictive approach to state data collection, which strengthens the position that the party votes No for its own reservation.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights against the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance and restrictions on freedom of religion.
Protect and further develop the individual's rights

motivering: Centerpartiet's election manifesto places climate and sustainable development at the center and requires capable leadership in these issues, which the Agenda 2030 communication represents. The Finance Committee's proposal to note the communication is a standard approval of the work carried out, consistent with C's support for the sustainability agenda. Rejecting the Left Party's claims (a socialist left-leaning approach) is consistent with C's stated non-socialist line.

citations.quote: Centerpartiet puts climate first, because the future must be green.
Economic growth and ambitious environmental and climate work must in practice go hand in hand
We prioritize long-term, common solutions with parties from both left and right

motivering: Centerpartiet is in opposition to the Tidö government (Tidöregeringen), which is supported by the Sweden Democrats — a collaboration the party explicitly rejects in the manifesto. The manifesto establishes that the work-first principle (arbetslinjen) shall be protected and that "more money shall be put into the core of welfare, less on benefits," which points toward the party's own budget alternative for the expenditure area. The party votes No against the government's proposal.

citations.quote: Centerpartiet is now the only bourgeois party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed. We stand firm on that.
More money shall be put into the core of welfare, less on benefits.
The work-first principle must be protected, and someone who can work shall not live on taxpayers' money.
citations.princip: the work-first principle in sickness insurance

motivering: The party's documents do not address gambling regulation or cash registers for amusement games. Centerpartiet has, however, submitted its own motion in the matter (Catarina Deremar et al., C, claim 1) which the committee rejects in favor of the government's proposal. The fact that the party has a reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 3) means it votes No to uphold its own position rather than supporting a proposal that dismisses their motion.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural areas. We shall clear up among superfluous rules and bureaucracy.
citations.princip: simplification of rules and reduction of bureaucracy

citations.quote: It shall be easy to start and run a company; it should be worth taking the leap and investing.
citations.princip: business-friendly and easy to run a company

motivering: Centerpartiet supports EU cooperation and is clearly against protectionism, which argues for implementing the EU directive on copyright in the digital single market. That newspaper companies shall be able to receive compensation when their material is reused online is consistent with the party's commitment to a viable and independent media coverage. The documents provide no support for deviating from the directive's implementation, which is why C should support the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
Comprehensive, independent and viable media coverage throughout the country is crucial for democracy. Press freedom shall be protected and independent public service defended.

motivering: Centerpartiet has put forward its own guidelines for economic policy (Annie Lööf et al., C, claim 1) which the committee's majority rejects. According to the election manifesto, C does not cooperate with SD or give them influence over governance, which is why the government's budget frameworks (supported by SD) cannot be supported with Yes. Reservation 1 does not represent C's own economic lines. Abstaining marks the party's own position.

citations.quote: Centerpartiet is now the only bourgeois party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.
We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, private savings or make housing more expensive.
The fiscal policy framework shall be protected and strengthened, and Sweden's long-term economic stability shall be defended.

motivering: Centerpartiet strongly prioritizes national security and a robust defense against Russia's aggression, which clearly argues for criminalizing foreign espionage. The pending constitutional process — with a mandatory vote after the election — is exactly the kind of raised threshold for constitutional amendment that C advocates. The restrictions on the right to communicate information to the media (meddelarfriheten) are narrowly targeted against foreign espionage and weigh lightly against the security policy need; the press freedom principle does not protect intelligence activities for foreign powers.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot exclude Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defense of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up against despots.
We want to make it harder to change the constitution, protect the position of the opposition in the Riksdag and strengthen the independence of the courts.
Press freedom shall be protected and independent public service defended.

omvarld.effekt: Strengthens the security arguments for criminalizing foreign espionage and protecting state secrets
Reinforces the need for clear legal protection against foreign intelligence activities

motivering: Centerpartiet's documents contain no specific commitment to gambling regulation or marketing of gambling. The party's pervasive liberal deregulation line — to clear away unnecessary rules and protect economic and social freedom for the individual — argues for supporting the committee's position to reject further marketing restrictions. The committee's proposal is in line with the party's freedom-oriented basic view.

citations.quote: Centerpartiet will always fight for a freer Sweden where people can decide more over their own lives. For that to succeed, more economic and social freedom is required
Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural areas. We shall clear up among superfluous rules and bureaucracy.
It shall be easy to start and run a company; it should be worth taking the leap and investing.

motivering: Centerpartiet emphasizes that processing times for the exercise of public authority must be shortened and that property rights shall be strengthened — principles that directly concern the efficiency of property formation at the Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority (Lantmäteriet). Rejecting the motions and noting the communication means that the Riksdag does not push through concrete demands based on the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) recommendations. The party advocates active pressure on public authorities and simplification of rules for rural areas, which is why No is the right vote.
